Chapter 3 – The Pump House

The pump house had been silent for nine years when Corvin forced the door.

Inside, the great iron wheel stood rusted in place, its spokes furred with orange scale.

He set his lamp on a crate and listened to the water dripping somewhere below.

Nothing answered him except the slow tick of the drops, steady as a clock that had forgotten what hour it was keeping.

“Hello?” he called, feeling foolish.

The echo came back thin and wrong, as though the room were much larger than it looked.

He found the ladder behind the wheel, its rungs slick with moss, and began to climb down into the dark one careful step at a time.

At the bottom the floor was ankle deep in cold water, and something pale was floating near the far wall.

It was a paper boat, perfectly dry, with his own name written on its sail in his mother’s tidy hand.
